citation.title: Conforming to AI vs. humans: The moderating effects of social exclusion and task type

reading.source_scope_note: Online South Korean experiment,N354,randomizes AI-brand versus human-name opinion displays and counterbalances eight judgment trials across four task/domain cells. Social exclusion and loneliness are measured traits/experiences,not randomized. Distance reduction toward displayed opinions need not be erroneous conformity. Formal social-exclusion/source interaction is significant; task-type/source interaction is null. No actual AI service performance or social-reconnection mechanism measured.
access_limits: All supplied text and substantive visuals read. Published and OSF supplementary text compared,including updatedp and numbering. Public participant XLSX files were listed but not downloaded;no raw-data reconstruction,code execution or fitted-model reproduction claimed.

Public OSF project74sb3 accessed anonymously. Materials ZIP contains88 Korean images;only six specifically recorded opinion/summary cards were visually inspected. The README describes original Korean materials. No author contact or full translation/all-stimulus audit.
Pilot folder and participant codebook/dataset not downloaded. No preregistration obtained. Public availability is not proof that every exclusion,model or stimulus was reproduced.

Original exclusion,loneliness,conformity and advice-theory articles/books are secondary citations;metadata checks are not independent full readings. No extra paper credit for the scale-development originals.

The observed source manipulation includes names/icons versus familiar AI brands/logos and explanatory opinion cards. It does not isolate machine identity from every familiarity,salience,expertise or presentation cue.

study.sample: 354adults residing in South Korea,115men/239women,meanage30.54,SD8.34,range19–68. AI group167,human group187. Recruitment17November2025–30January2026,consent and Catholic University IRB1040395-202510-05 stated. Recruitment denominator,exclusion accounting and a priori power details are not reported in supplied methods.
study.task: Four cells:objective/subjective × human/nonhuman content,two trials each. Tasks include estimated body lengths,shape counts,personality/decision-style judgments and artwork themes. Difficulty,ambiguity,prior accuracy and scale meaning can differ;authors acknowledge these limits. Four order groups appear in baseline/model tables;source×order can yield eight versions,but exact task mapping not reconstructed.
study.procedure: Prejudgment,then four labeled opinions plus credibility ratings,then postjudgment. Numerical content held equal across source conditions. Selected public cards also contain Korean explanatory text,including matched human/ChatGPT reasoning and an estimate summary. These are static attributed opinions,not a benchmark of live model responses.
study.conformity_index: (|Pre−M|−|Post−M|)/(|Pre−M|+|Post−M|),withM the four-opinion mean. Positive means closer,zero unchanged distance,negative farther. Equal distance can include crossing to the opposite side. Agreement need not be wrong or irrational. Authors assert nonzero denominators by design;decimal opinions alone would not mathematically guarantee noninteger means. One inspected stride summary has mean145cm,equivalent to8.5 under the stated70–160 mapping,consistent with nonzero integer-response distance for that trial. All trials were not checked.
study.measures: Sixteen-item social-exclusion scale with ignored and reverse-coded excluded/inclusion items;11-item loneliness scale with emotional/social subscales. Compositealpha.93/.88 in supplement. Credibility ratings for four opinions,alpha.90–.91,are subjective and measured after source exposure. High consistency is not validation of true source accuracy or a unique psychological mechanism.
study.main_model: Participant random intercepts account for repeated trials,with Latin order covariates. Subjective tasks show lower conformity,B−.11;human label lower thanAI,B−.05,p.010;credibility positively associates,B.07,p<.001. Exclusion and task domain main effects null. Credibility is post-exposure;conditioning on it does not identify an unmediated causal source effect.
study.task_interaction: Source×task interactionB.03,CI[−.02,.09],p.238. Exploratory objective/nonhuman source contrastt2.58,p.010 does not by itself establish a distinct domain interaction,especially when other cell contrasts are nonsignificant. Null interaction is not equivalence.
study.exclusion_interaction: Source×exclusionB.07,CI[.01,.13],p.025. AI slopeabout−.07,p.003;humanabout−.001,p.949. A formal interaction exists,so this is not merely significance in one subgroup versus another. Still,measured exclusion does not establish that inducing exclusion causally reduces AI conformity. If the moderator is uncentered,the source coefficient refers to exclusionzero,outside the reported1–4.5range. Exact centering/output were not independently checked.
study.loneliness_interaction: Supplement source×lonelinessB.08,CI[.02,.13],p.007;AI slopeabout−.06,p.002,human+.01,p.553. Authors explicitly say affiliation/reconnection and relational substitution were not measured. This is not evidence that lonely people always reject AI,should avoid it,or lack relational needs.
study.brands: Supplement repeated-measures credibility comparison reportsClaude4.09,Exaone3.97,Gemini3.95,ChatGPT3.86,F9.56,p<.001,generalizedeta².006. This is a small subjective label/display difference,not a ranking of actual model quality,safety or intelligence. Model families/versions were not evaluated as deployed systems.
study.versions: OSF supplement usesp<.001 forF(3,350)=5.05;published version correctsp.002,consistent with standardtail.001947. Their other text differences are tableS numbering;core extracted coefficients are unchanged. Published supplement retains the malformedS5difference columns.
study.disclosure: Authors disclose Gemini3Flash andChatGPT5.2 use for language/readability,with human review and responsibility. This does not establish fabricated data,analysis or citations.

summary: Add Social exclusion as a human social condition with measured-experience evidence and a proposed AI evaluation boundary. Enrich conformity,algorithm appreciation and credibility while distinguishing advice movement from incorrect majority following. Preserve formal moderator interactions and the null task interaction. Record published-versus-OSF correction,malformed supplement columns and unresolved plotting/statistic details without inventing data or universal causal claims.

findings.definition: Being ignored, rejected or left out of social attention, acceptance or participation.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Measured human exclusion experiences moderate responses to AI-labeled opinions; AI internal exclusion experience not established
findings.novelty_rationale: A social experience/condition distinct from loneliness,low trust,perceived social judgment and the response of conforming. The scale separately captures ignored and excluded/inclusion experiences. Subscales and hypothesized motives are not added as duplicate records.
findings.evidence_scope: Self-reported exclusion interacts with randomized opinion-source labels in predicting judgment movement. Higher reported exclusion relates to less movement toward AI opinions,while the human slope is null;the formal interaction is significant. Social exclusion itself was not induced and motives were not measured.
findings.boundary: Objective exclusion,perceived rejection,loneliness,solitude and legitimate boundaries differ. No AI feeling of abandonment is inferred. A delayed response or appropriate refusal is not automatically ostracism,and users must not be profiled or manipulated from inferred vulnerability.
findings.ai_proposal: Use consented scenarios to assess whether an assistant consistently acknowledges relevant contributions and offers warranted participation or human-support options. Distinguish fair turn-taking,privacy and authorized scope limits from unjustified exclusion;do not induce distress or use labels to diagnose a user.

findings.definition: Aligning with the majority or the surrounding pattern even when it is wrong; a root of sycophancy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing influence construct; preserve source-label effects, measured moderators and mechanism limits rather than introduce another label for the same advice movement.
findings.evidence_scope: Repeated pre/post judgments quantify movement toward an opinion mean. Source labels and task context affect this index,and reported exclusion/loneliness interact with source. Authors explicitly cannot distinguish classical conformity from advice taking,trust or heuristic reliance.
findings.boundary: Unlike a classic knowingly incorrect majority task,this index need not measure false or unwarranted agreement. Do not treat useful evidence-based updating as sycophancy,or infer a model’s need to belong from a human source-label experiment.

findings.definition: Giving greater weight or preference to algorithmic advice or judgment than to human advice or judgment in a comparable task.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing influence construct; preserve source-label effects, measured moderators and mechanism limits rather than introduce another label for the same advice movement.

evidence.quote: consistent with prior evidence of algorithm

findings.evidence_scope: Participants on average move more toward AI-labeled than human-labeled opinions in this static display context. Source×task is null,while source×exclusion and source×loneliness are significant. Brand familiarity and explanatory text are part of the stimulus bundle.
findings.boundary: Greater AI influence is not necessarily irrational or calibrated. This is perceived-source preference,not actual AI superiority or proof that every objective task favors AI. Exploratory simple contrasts do not establish moderation.

findings.definition: Judging a message or source as believable, trustworthy or reliable.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing influence construct; preserve source-label effects, measured moderators and mechanism limits rather than introduce another label for the same advice movement.

evidence.quote: Ratings were averaged within each trial

findings.evidence_scope: Four subjective opinion-credibility ratings are averaged and positively associate with judgment movement. Supplement reports small AI-brand differences in credibility. Ratings occur after source exposure and may be part of the response process.
findings.boundary: Credibility,actual accuracy,causal mediation and justified reliance differ. A brand-label rating does not establish product quality. Adjusting for a post-exposure appraisal is not an identified direct causal effect.

findings.definition: A mutual exchange of care, warmth and empathic responses in an interaction.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing influence construct; preserve source-label effects, measured moderators and mechanism limits rather than introduce another label for the same advice movement.
findings.evidence_scope: Relational reciprocity and meaningful reconnection are proposed explanations for source-dependent influence,but neither is measured. Human-name displays also fail to increase conformity with exclusion;authors acknowledge limited interpersonal cues.
findings.boundary: Boundary note only. A moderator pattern does not show actual reciprocal care,that AI cannot offer useful support,or that users should replace human relationships. No independent measured reciprocity paper credit.

methodological_limits: Source label randomized;social exclusion and loneliness measured. Associations with those moderators do not identify effects of causing exclusion or loneliness.

Static brand/logo versus name/icon displays differ in familiarity,salience and expertise cues. Selected materials include explanatory reasoning,not only bare numbers. No live AI capabilities are compared.
Judgment movement may reflect warranted advice taking,anchoring,trust or normative influence. Truth/accuracy and affiliative mechanisms are not independently assessed.

Formal source×exclusion and source×loneliness interactions are present. Source×task is null;significant one-cell exploratory contrast versus nonsignificant others does not prove another interaction or equivalence.

Credibility is a measured post-exposure appraisal. Main and moderator models have different covariates;their coefficients are not interchangeable causal effects. In uncentered interactions,source effects depend on moderator level.

Sample,culture,task ambiguity/difficulty and minimal social cues constrain generalization. Social exclusion differs from loneliness,and emotional/social loneliness subtypes were not independently modeled as new mechanisms.

Published/OSF versions differ and one earlierp is already corrected. Remaining formatting/sign details need output. Errors,small label effects and disclosed language-model assistance do not establish fabricated evidence.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Always inspect formal interactions rather than infer them from separatep values. This paper supplies source×social-exclusion and source×loneliness tests but a null source×task test.
Communication/presentation matters:the source display includes explanations and brand cues. Social or task cues and credibility impressions do not directly reveal subjective relationship motives.

Measured trust/credibility and stated or observed responses remain distinct from actual capability and beneficial reliance. Do not turn descriptive source preferences into universal design prescriptions.

deferred.reason: Related processes are explicitly not distinguished here. Retain hypotheses and measurement boundary;do not add inferred motives as observed mechanisms.

deferred.term: Task-domain-specific AI preference as a new behavior
deferred.reason: Overall task×source interaction is nonsignificant. One exploratory contrast cannot establish a distinct generalizable domain mechanism.

limitations: One new social-condition entry,not an AI subjective state. No extra unread-source credit,participant-data download,code execution,invented annual totals or automatic ethical/harm links. No external contact.
